title: Generate random anisotropy axes
action: Set up a 64×64 square lattice with periodic boundary conditions and assign a random unit easy axis to each site, drawn uniformly on the circle.
description: This configuration defines the quenched disorder for all subsequent simulations.

title: Hysteresis loop M(H) at D/J=0.4, T/J=0.1
action: Run single‑spin‑flip Metropolis Monte Carlo field‑cycling simulation with D/J=0.4, T/J=0.1, sweeping the external field from H/J=-2 to H/J=+2 (and back) using at least 10⁵ MC cycles per field point. Extract the magnetisation per spin M at each field and write the complete loop.
description: CSV containing the field H and magnetisation M for the full hysteresis loop. The loop must enclose a non‑zero area.
output_schema: Columns: H (float), M (float). At least 100 rows covering both sweep directions.

title: Coercive field H_co vs temperature
action: For each temperature T/J in {0.1,0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9,1.0,1.1,1.2} at D/J=0.4, run a field‑cycling simulation as above. From the resulting M(H) loop determine the coercive field H_co (the field at which M changes sign) and output one row per temperature.
description: CSV reporting the coercive field at each temperature, derived from simulated hysteresis loops.
output_schema: Columns: temperature (T/J, float), coercive_field (H_co/J, float). One row per temperature, sorted by increasing T.

title: Magnetisation M(T) from quench‑reheating protocol
action: Start from a random spin configuration at high temperature. Quench to T=0, then warm up in steps of ΔT≈0.1 from T=0 to T=1.5. At each temperature, equilibrate using at least 10⁴ MC cycles and measure the average magnetisation M at zero applied field. Write the collected M(T) data.
description: CSV containing the temperature and ensemble‑averaged magnetisation from the quench‑reheating procedure.
output_schema: Columns: temperature (T/J, float), magnetization (M, float). One row per temperature step from 0 to 1.5.

title: Long relaxation from aligned initial state
action: Starting from a perfectly aligned spin configuration (all spins pointing in the same direction), run single‑spin‑flip Metropolis Monte Carlo for 10^6 MC cycles at several temperatures in the range 0.1–1.5. Record the time evolution of magnetisation and the final spin configuration to study memory effects.
description: Long‑time relaxation runs from aligned state to document the four temperature regimes (glassified, intermediate, KT algebraic, disordered).
output_schema: Columns: temperature (float), final_magnetization (float), memory_observable (float). Optional evidence log.

title: Finite‑size scaling for Kosterlitz–Thouless transition temperature
action: Perform finite‑size scaling analysis to determine the Kosterlitz–Thouless transition temperature T_KT. Run Metropolis simulations for system sizes L = 16, 32, 64 at D/J=0.4 and zero field, using the spin‑wave stiffness or Binder cumulant crossing method. Document the extracted T_KT.
description: Evidence from finite‑size scaling analysis documenting the Kosterlitz–Thouless transition temperature determination.
